results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 68 body units match the controlling idea of the spec paragraph aligned to them, in spec order; the five introduction callouts are callouts and match no spec paragraph. The one unit the outliner marked with two ideas (Architecture ¶10) states the two consequences of price tools that the spec paragraph p28 itself declares.

Only Architecture ¶10 was marked with two ideas. It opens 'Two architectural consequences follow' and its spec paragraph (p28) declares exactly those two consequences of price tools as one controlling idea, so the paragraph has one umbrella idea. No other unit needed two summaries.
results.draft_locus: Architecture: A Workspace Over Systems of Record ¶10

results.finding: Every unit ties to a supporting claim: Concepts and the worked-example Golf units to S1, the workspace and account units to S2, the partner-API, trade-off and Chief Architect units to S3, the neutrality, Keybridge and exit-economics units to S4; failure modes, questions and conclusion restate S1-S4.

All five tables and five figures carry captions that say what they show, and the quotations and statistics elsewhere (OLX, Rightmove, Autotrader partner scale, mobile.de, CarGurus, RFC 9700, P2B articles, Scout24/Zillow/Cox/Cars.com, Vinted, Deal Builder pause, ChatGPT apps) are framed by a claim sentence they support, except the case below.

results.draft_locus: Architecture: A Workspace Over Systems of Record ¶8
results.quote: shows the direction.
results.finding: The Buying Signals quotation closes the paragraph with 'shows the direction' and no sentence says what it shows (that model scores now ride on the exported lead and must be explainable). Flow reader A reported being 'unsure what direction the Buying Signals example shows'.

Every declared transition_in is expressed at its boundary and picks up the declared known information: section openers name Ingrid's first, second and third questions; 'Bulk operations follow the same rule' (similarity); 'Three design rules follow', 'Two architectural consequences follow' (cause_effect); 'Whatever happens to the regulation' and 'The controls cost something' (contrast); 'Keybridge is one of three ways', 'Which option fits also depends on the vertical' (elaboration); 'Preventing these failures takes' (cause_effect); 'Those measures will soon cover' (time); 'Part III's supply chain is now complete' (conclusion_summary).

results.quote: The productscape reference model (the author's domain model) of a general listings marketplace, a generic model and not a description of any company, gives its professional-merchant persona three jobs
results.finding: Both flow readers had to re-read the sentence that answers 'what professionals need': two stacked qualifications sit between subject and verb, and 'productscape' arrives with only a parenthetical gloss. Splitting the sentence would fix it.

results.draft_locus: Architecture: A Workspace Over Systems of Record ¶10
results.quote: exactly the kind of aggregated data whose access the EU's Platform-to-Business Regulation asks portals to describe (see below)
results.finding: Both flow readers stopped at the forward reference: the P2B Regulation is named only in a callout and explained two sections later, so the reader has to hold it in mind. Either give the one-clause gist here or drop the pointer.

results.quote: as with Autotrader's Deal Builder rollout pause in late 2025 (see Failure Modes)
results.finding: Table 5 cites the Deal Builder rollout pause before anything explains it, and points two sections ahead; both readers met the event without context. Say in the cell what the pause was, or drop the forward reference.

results.quote: **Rolling out platform-controlled states without consent.**
results.finding: Both readers found this the one failure mode no body section prepared: platform-controlled states (reserved flags, automatic price suggestions, AI agents answering buyers) first appear in a Table 5 cell and then here, and become review question 10. The spec's Architecture section has no paragraph on per-organization configuration of automated actions, so the order itself introduces new material in the failure list.
results.corroborated_by: flow-B item 14 (same problem; flow-A item 13, second half)

results.quote: Owning SaaS also changes the economics of a group exit.
results.finding: Both readers stumbled on this paragraph: reader A found divestment a new consideration nothing had prepared, tacked onto the trade-off rule; reader B did not know what 'group exit' meant until the next sentence. The opening sentence should say plainly what is meant (selling or keeping a business separately) and tie it to separate tenancy.

Terms on does_not_know are given before use: pro tooling, lead management for pros and pro SaaS in Introduction ¶3; the lead ledger and performance read model in the Figure 2 caption and pieces list; the lead lifecycle in Figure 1; P2B Articles 7 and 9 and the four controls in the Neutrality section (P2B is named and glossed in the KEY POINTS callout before its forward mention in Architecture ¶10, recorded under flow_is_followable). Veldmark cast, the Golf, the Lyon apartment, failure-pattern names and the vertical layer model are on already_knows.

The introduction opens on an intriguing example (the private seller against the dealer who lives in the marketplace), bridges to the reconciliation test, defines its terms and gives a roadmap; none of placeholder, restated question, dictionary, 'dawn of man' or book report.

The closing does not open with 'in conclusion', adds no new subtopic or body evidence (the 90-second and 10-second targets are recalled from publication-pipeline as declared), and ends on a hand-off to search-architecture rather than a rephrased thesis.

From Supply to Discovery ¶1 states what no single section states, that Part III's five chapters form one chain ending at the professional's reconciliation; ¶2 gives the so-what for discovery (indices as read models; a missing link leaves Part IV the ghost, the duplicate or the disputed count).

The closing returns to the hook ('it ends where this chapter began: with professionals who judge the marketplace by whether its numbers agree with their own'), to both scene arguments (Ruhrblick's withdrawn downgrade, Claire's question answered with checkable controls) and to the part's 'one chain, not five features'.

From the callouts and the four opening paragraphs alone, the cold reader predicted the opening case with both arguments, what professionals need (outcomes over exposure through to the lead from their side), the workspace architecture, neutrality with the four controls and the P2B Regulation, the worked example settling both arguments, build/integrate/own, vertical differences, failure modes, the Chief Architect's view and review questions, in that order, with evidence from company filings and product documentation, EU law and the fictional Veldmark. This matches the roadmap and AC-2's expected answer.

The cold reader rebuilt the Golf's counts per channel from one ledger: 19 unique buyers after deduplicating 23 raw contacts, the CRM's 14 explained by e-mail-only export, a VIN match to the sale; then raw and deduplicated counts side by side, Lead API and webhooks for every channel with stable IDs and deduplication keys, opt-in sale matching by VIN, and statistics on the same event stream as billing. It refused the CEO's request, aggregated or anonymized, kept the report inside the CRM per agency, and named separate tenancy, API parity, the data boundary and ranking blindness with an evidence pack for an annual independent review. All elements of AC-1's expected answer are present.
